steps.title: 1. Problem analysis and links to the curriculum
steps.description:
We must evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx.
• Givens: integrand f(x)=x sin(2x); limits 0 and π/8.
Relevant syllabus areas:
• “Integration — Continued: find integrals using integration by parts.” The integrand is a product of an algebraic function (x) and a trigonometric function (sin 2x), the classic setting for integration by parts.
• We also use the trigonometric identity that integrates sin (2x) into −½ cos (2x) (Functions & Differentiation: use identities, standard derivatives/integrals).
steps.hints: Recall the integration-by-parts formula: ∫ u dv = u v − ∫ v du. Choose u so that du simplifies the integrand.

steps.title: 2. Choose u and dv for integration by parts
steps.description:
Let
u = x  → du = dx,
dv = sin(2x) dx → v = ∫ sin(2x) dx = −½ cos(2x).
steps.hints: Differentiate the algebraic factor and integrate the trigonometric factor.

steps.title: 3. Apply the integration-by-parts formula
steps.description: ∫ x sin(2x) dx = u v − ∫ v du = x(−½ cos 2x) − ∫ (−½ cos 2x) dx = −½ x cos 2x + ½ ∫ cos 2x dx.
steps.hints: Carry the minus sign carefully; remember that −∫(−½ cos 2x) = +(½)∫cos 2x.

steps.title: 4. Complete the indefinite integral
steps.description:
∫ cos 2x dx = ½ sin 2x, so
∫ x sin(2x) dx = −½ x cos 2x + ½·½ sin 2x + C = −(x/2) cos 2x + (1/4) sin 2x + C.
steps.hints: Review the standard integral ∫ cos(kx) dx = (1/k) sin(kx).

steps.title: 5. Evaluate between the limits 0 and π/8

final_solution:
The definite integral equals
∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx = √2 (4 − π) / 32.
